# RESCRAPE LEDGER — which loaders can re-run, how often, safely, and what they drop

     This is the document that goes stale first: it describes 300+ moving objects. -->

> **337 registered objects.** Every figure below is read from the warehouse and from
> the loader sources on disk at build time. Rebuild with `python scripts/build_rescrape_ledger.py`.

## What the operator asked, and the four answers

> *"I would like to know exactly which loaders can be rerun to rescrape all of our data and
> append it for new observations and which ones can't, and why… we scraped only partial data
> (only some columns) for most datasets, and we want to ensure that EVERY column is grabbed
> upon rescrape."*

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| Which can I re-run here? | **139** name a script that exists on disk |
| Which are somebody else's? | **131** are clips of `energy.*` — the re-run is a re-clip and `energy` is READ-ONLY to this workstream |
| Which cannot be re-run at all? | **49** honestly unresolved + **2** with no command + **0** whose command names a script that is not on disk |
| Which are unsafe to re-run? | **2** read their own output while replacing it — see §3 |

## 1. APPEND vs REPLACE — can this be re-run *safely*?

⛔ **A command that can be re-run is not the same as one that can be re-run safely.** Most
builds here are `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, which discards history — right for a clip, wrong
for an observation series where the whole point is to accumulate.

| verdict | n | what it means for a refresh |
|---|---|---|
| `replace_safe` | 129 | rebuilds from source; re-running cannot double-count |
| `append_only` | 3 | ⚠ accumulates. Re-running **adds** rows — right for a series, a defect for a snapshot |
| `delegated` | 131 | a re-clip owned by the platform session |
| `not_idempotent` | 0 | ⛔ do not re-run without reading the loader first |
| `unknown` | 74 | no write of this table found in the named loader |

⚠ **The shape of the append defect, paid for on 2026-08-20b:** `build_gas_facilities.py`
appended to a payload it did not own and took compressor features 24 → 48 and storage 22 → 44
on one re-run. Valid GeoJSON, no error, every count overstated exactly 2×.

## 2. CADENCE — how often is there anything new to get?

⛔ **`in_refresh_cadence` exists and is not enough.** Measured: it derives a cadence for **16**
of its 268 rows and answers *"cannot derive — the source publishes no event date"* for the
other 252. It asks the DATA when the question is about the PUBLISHER. The Drought Monitor is
weekly whether or not our copy carries a date column.

| cadence | n |
|---|---|
| `unknown` | 133 |
| `on the platform re-clip` | 122 |
| `monthly` | 27 |
| `quarterly` | 18 |
| `event-driven` | 12 |
| `annual` | 11 |
| `as-revised` | 5 |
| `as-filed` | 5 |
| `weekly` | 3 |
| `continuous` | 1 |

⚠ `unknown` is reported rather than defaulted. A wrong refresh schedule is worse than an
absent one: it invites a re-run that costs money and returns the same rows.

## 3. ⛔ LOADERS THAT READ THEIR OWN OUTPUT — re-run these only after reading them

A build that SELECTs from the table it also replaces is not idempotent in practice, even
though its write mode looks safe. **This is not theoretical.** `build_land_gates.py` measured
`in_tribal_land.geom`, then replaced that table with the geometry column renamed `geog` — so
every run after the first died with *"Unrecognized name: geom"*. It had been unrunnable for a
day while its registry row advertised a working command. Fixed 2026-08-20d; found only because
G122 forced a rebuild of everything downstream of `in_screener_candidates`.

| object | loader |
|---|---|
| `in_substations` | `repair_substation_geometry.py` |
| `in_tribal_land` | `build_land_gates.py` |

## 4. ⭐ FULL-COLUMN CAPTURE — what every clip is leaving behind

The operator is right that we took partial slices. For every object whose registry names an
`energy.*` parent, our column list is compared against the parent's.

⚠ **A dropped column is not automatically a defect** — a clip that deliberately keeps five
columns of a 200-column parent is a decision. What was never a decision is a cut by POSITION:
`build_gas_facilities.py` sliced the parent schema at `[:10]` and silently dropped `operator`,
`owner`, `status`, `county`, `ownerpct` and `reservname`, because a positional cut keeps
whatever the publisher happened to put first.
